ECC: Genetic Tools — How to Optimize AI Agents for Software Engineering

The video features ECC, a set of open source tools to organize the work of code assistants with AI. Displays the components (subagents, skills, hooks and rules), the cycle of planning, testing, reviewing, remembering and improving, memory between sessions, security check with AgentShield and team plans.

What is ECC

The video deals with ECC, which he presents as "Everything Claude Code": a complete framework that changes the way code assistants with AI work 00:00. The video cites over 1 million ECC skill installations in 30 days 00:21.

In addition to basic prompts

When programming with AI, at first everything seems magical, but soon the AI forgets the context and ignores the process 01:03. Video compares structureless AI to a brilliant but chaotic junior developer: fast, inconsistent and memoryless 01:25. ECC flows work as a disciplined engineering manager: they bring structure, persistent memory and limits to keep code safe 01:46.

ECC is not a configuration file: it functions as an operating system for the agent environment, with ready skills, planning, memory optimization and security 02:08. The video cites more than 140,000 stars and 21,000 forks at GitHub, an award on Anthropic's hackathon and documentation in more than 12 languages, including Portuguese 02:29.

The components

ECC power comes from a modular ecosystem, not from a giant prompt 02:50. The numbers below are those quoted in the video 03:10:

  • 68 specialized subagents, such as an architect or a security analyst, to delegate each task to the right profile 03:10;
  • 293 skills, ready and reusable workflows 03:10;
  • hooks, automations shooting alone during execution 03:10;
  • mandatory rules, separated by programming language 03:31.

Together, rules, hooks and skills make the model follow the path, check their own work and fix the code without having to ask 03:31.

Despite its name, ECC functions as a universal layer: in addition to Claude Code, it runs with Codex, Cursor, Gemini and OpenCode 04:13.

The cycle of agentic engineering

ECC makes AI follow a five-step cycle 04:35:

1. Planning architecture before writing code 04:35. 2. Test and implement in a TDD flow 04:35. 3. Review and verify with quality gates 04:564. 4. Remember decisions with unified memory 04:56. 5. Improve by extracting session patterns 04:56.

In the terminal, this becomes bar commands 04:56. /plan Call the planning agent, /tdd Call the test guide, /code-review calls the quality subagent and /build-fix calls the build error solver 05:18.

Memory and security

Unified memory attacks context amnesia: agents save what they have done, search the project history and maintain conversation between sessions 05:39. If the chat window closes, nothing critical gets lost 06:00.

With agents who have persistent access to the project, the question arises: what can they access 06:00? ? AgentShield checks configuration security 06:21. According to the video, it runs 102 static analysis rules and over 1,200 tests 06:21. It reads prompts and settings and ensures that secrets, such as API keys, are not exposed 06:42.

For teams

Video describes three levels 07:02:

  • the open source layer, free, for those who work alone and run local streams 07:02;
  • GitHub App or Pro plans for private repositories and teams, at $19 per seat per month 07:02;
  • the tailor-made Enterprise plan with dedicated deployment and training 07:24.

The video quotes an Amazon engineering leader: an engineer thought a team of 10 to 15 people was working on what one person did with the tools 07:24.

Final reflection

The final question: Today's AI configuration looks like a chaotic junior who needs supervision all the time, or a predictable and disciplined engineering team 08:05?

Nope. According to the video, it also runs with Codex, Cursor, Gemini and OpenCode 04:13.

What cycle does the ECC impose?

Plan, test and implement, review, remember and improve 04:35.

About the video

In this video, we explore the **ECC (Everything Claude Code)**, the operational layer and open source toolkit created by **Affaan Mustafa (`affaan-m`)** to optimize the performance of AI encoding agents.

Learn how ECC turns AI assistants — such as **Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode** — into a disciplined software engineering system. We approach the architecture of **specialized subagents**, **reusable skills**, **automation by hooks**, **persistent memory** and security audits with **AgentShield**.

-**00:00** — Introduction to ECC and the concept of Agentic engineering
